title: Organisations urge Karnataka govt to be prepared to face Super El Nino conditions in 2027 - Deccan Herald
full_text:
Bengaluru: The All India Central Council for Trade Unions (AICCTU), Bangalore Environment Forum (BEF) and Fridays For Future - Karnataka (FFF-K) have urged the state to be prepared for the Super El Nino conditions expected in 2027.
In a statement, the organisations pointed out that a combination of climate change and El Nino has made the World Meteorological Organization to warn that 2027 could be the hottest year since records began.
“According to news reports, Karnataka, in particular, is projected to witness 1,900 additional heat related deaths. This is not counting the impacts of the super El Nino on the agrarian economy. Karnataka is already facing conditions of drought which will only worsen with El Nino. In cities like Bengaluru, which are already water-stressed, the coming El Nino will compound the water crises. Indeed, as research has shown, the brunt of climate-related crises are felt disproportionately by the working urban poor as well as slum communities and other informal settlements in cities,” the statement noted.
The representatives also that it is important to acknowledge that many of the workers and communities, including municipal safaikaramcharis, sanitation workers, construction workers, rural agricultural workers, ASHA and Anganwadi workers, street vendors, gig workers, livestock-dependent households, fisherpeople, nomadic communities, among others are exposed to extreme heat while working outdoors
The organisation urged that the State Government must act and prepare for the coming months now. The first step, they said, was to identify districts, communities and working people most exposed to heat and water stress. The government should also enforce and implement advisories and Karnataka High Court judgments related to climate change and heat waves. “Similarly the Government has to comply with its heatwave action plan and the judgment of the Karnataka High Court in W.P. No. 8683/2025 and implement the circulars referenced therein. This must also be made applicable to private sector employers. The government must also ensure timely micro-level weather alerts, shaded rest areas, ensuring access to cool drinking water and mandating regular breaks during peak heat hours,” the statement said.
They also demanded that the state must, under the provisions of Disaster Management Act, 2005, declare ex-sgratia compensation for persons affected by heatwaves and should strengthen hospital preparedness for heat-related emergencies.
